5-6: Taking 1 or 2 stones in turn: who takes the last stone with the right play.
Taking 1, 2 or 3 matches when the one who takes the last match loses.
Taking from a pile only amounts of a fixed set, such as 1, 3 or 4: a table of winning and losing positions.
Two piles of coins, any number taken from one pile in turn: equal piles and who wins.
Breaking a bar into small squares in turn: the number of breaks is fixed, so who makes the last.
Signs plus and minus put in turn between numbers: whether the result is odd or even is fixed before the game starts.
A king moved towards a corner of a board in turn: the squares to leave the other player on.
Coins in a row, one taken from either end in turn: how the first player makes sure of at least half.
Symmetry: copying the other player's moves, such as coins placed on a round table, to win.
Writing the digits of a three-digit number in turn: whether the last player can make it divisible by 3.
